defects: The film is built like a slide deck: numbered chapter cards (02 / PROCESS, 03 / TASTING NOTES, 04 / ROAST) change in place, and there is no camera move and no transition idea between sections.
The animation is mostly sequential build-on: icons appear one at a time, beans fill one after another, and outlines draw on. Each section repeats the same reveal and adds no new kind of motion.
Dead air: 12 of 19 seconds look like the previous second. Headlines and labels stay frozen while one small element animates.
The scrubbing circle on the water stroke is a weak, UI-like gesture with no weight or follow-through. It reads as a cursor, not as water.
Frame 3 (a lone bergamot with large empty space) and other mid-build frames are not composed to stand alone.
The colour fills are offset from their outlines like misregistered print. This is consistent across the film, but the crescent-shaped gap in each fill looks like a mask artefact rather than a choice.
The soundtrack is a steady wall of percussive transients from start to finish. A brighter layer comes in near 10.5s, but there is no clear drop, breath or hit that lines up with the section changes.
gaps: Choreography and transitions. Each section is a static card being filled in. Top studio work would carry the contour line through the whole film, for example from origin map to water ripple to the rings of the fruit to the bean crease and back to the contour, so the scenes hand off through one continuous object instead of swapping cards.

Energy arc and spacing. The pace is flat and the reveals are evenly timed one after another, with no build toward a roast climax at 60-80% and no release. The film needs varied rhythm, overlap, and moves with real weight that settle, for example beans that drop and tumble instead of fading in.

Sound design and sync. The music is dense and evenly loud, with no hits written for the picture: no water, roast crackle or pour sounds, and no dynamic shape. Sound and picture feel laid side by side rather than locked together.
